prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
SNP Manifesto 2019 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core vision and constitutional position
- Put Scotland’s future in Scotland’s hands via an independence referendum (sought in 2020 through a lawful Section 30 transfer).
- Keep Scotland in, or aligned as closely as possible with, the EU; support a UK-wide second EU referendum with Remain on the ballot and revocation of Article 50 to stop no-deal.

Brexit, economy and public finances
- Oppose the Boris Johnson deal; protect access to the EU single market/customs union; build a progressive alliance to lock the Tories out.
- End austerity, reverse real-terms cuts to Scotland’s budget, invest in services and productivity, oppose VAT rises, crack down on tax avoidance/evasion, and seek devolution of tax and National Insurance.
- Support SMEs through Brexit advice, increase the Employment Allowance, deliver sector deals, fair city/region deals, and accelerate infrastructure via the Scottish National Investment Bank and improved broadband/5G.

Health, social security and living standards
- Call for UK per-capita NHS spending to match Scotland’s; legislate an NHS Protection Act to keep health services out of trade deals; compensate contaminated blood victims.
- Overhaul welfare: end the benefit freeze, Universal Credit roll‑out (halt and reform), sanctions regime, two‑child cap and rape clause; uplift income-replacement benefits at least by inflation; fair terminal illness rules; UK-wide take-up campaigns.
- Expand parental rights: longer, better-paid maternity/paternity/shared leave, neonatal leave, stronger anti-redundancy protections.
- Pensions: protect the triple lock; oppose state pension age increases; back WASPI fairness; restore Pension Credit and free TV licences; extend auto-enrolment; create a Savings & Pension Commission.
- Tackle drugs deaths: devolve drug policy and enable supervised consumption facilities.

Jobs, fair work and rights
- Seek devolution of employment law; raise the statutory living wage to the real Living Wage; end age discrimination; act on the gig economy; tougher equal pay enforcement.
- Strengthen consumer protections (fair delivery charges, cap on high‑cost credit, ticket touting), protect access to cash/banking, and regulate online harms with a new duty of care and independent regulator.

Climate and energy
- Match Scotland’s legal targets (75% emissions cut by 2030; net zero by 2045); align with EU standards post‑Brexit.
- Green Energy Deal: support renewables (onshore wind, solar, floating offshore, tidal), reform transmission charges, deliver island interconnectors, back CCS, oppose fracking and new nuclear, incentivise low‑carbon heat and ULEVs, greener tax reforms, major tree‑planting, zero‑emission rail by 2035, better bus infrastructure, faster Scotland–London rail, net‑zero aviation trials in the Highlands and Islands.

Rural, food, farming and fisheries
- Protect CAP replacement funding and deliver the full convergence uplift; defend standards and PGIs; mitigate tariffs; ensure fair seafood export processes; strengthen the Groceries Code Adjudicator.

Migration, asylum and citizenship
- Devolve immigration or create a Scottish Visa; oppose the hostile environment and £30k salary threshold; scrap indefinite detention; expand family reunion; give asylum seekers the right to work; scale up refugee resettlement.

Democracy, human rights and broadcasting
- Replace First Past the Post with STV; abolish the House of Lords; votes at 16 and for EU citizens with leave to remain; incorporate UNCRC; defend the ECHR; create an independent debates commission; devolve broadcasting and increase BBC Scotland’s share.

Defence, foreign policy and veterans
- Scrap Trident; shift spend to public services and conventional defence; keep UK aid at 0.7% with a Climate Justice Fund; support peace, human rights defenders and international law; house homeless veterans in vacant MoD homes; grant ILR to Commonwealth personnel.

Record at Westminster
- Helped block no-deal and unlawful prorogation; secured police/fire VAT relief; restored post‑study visas; unlocked farm payments; improved some UC elements; cut FOBT stakes; defended Scotch whisky.
